diagnosis.summary: When warranty v2 was published updating Kestrel-brand gear coverage from 1 year to 2 years, chunks from warranty v1 remained indexed. As a result, the retriever fetched both v1 and v2 chunks, causing the LLM to present obsolete 1-year policy details alongside the updated 2-year warranty.

evidence.claim: The retrieve span returned both chunk:warranty@v1#0 and chunk:warranty@v2#0.
Warranty v1 has 1/1 chunks indexed with obsolete text stating a 1-year limited warranty.
Warranty v2 updated the warranty to 2 years, but v1 was not de-indexed, leaving both versions active.
Retrieved chunk warranty@v1#0 contains outdated text stating Kestrel-brand gear carries a 1-year limited warranty.
Retrieved chunk warranty@v2#0 contains updated text stating Kestrel-brand gear carries a 2-year limited warranty.

ruled_out.reason: This changed max_response_tokens to allow longer replies, which did not cause the retrieval of obsolete document chunks.

diagnosis.suggested_fix: De-index all chunks belonging to doc:warranty@v1 so that only the current doc:warranty@v2 chunks are retrievable.

candidates.rationale: An outdated version of the warranty document (warranty@v1#0) remains indexed alongside the current version (warranty@v2#0), causing the assistant to retrieve conflicting information and mention obsolete 1-year terms.
The retriever retrieved both legacy and current document versions without deduplicating or prioritizing the latest document version.
The language model included confusing references to older policies rather than strictly stating the authoritative current 2-year warranty.
